segments.speaker: ROOSEVELT
segments.text: The CHAIRMAN said that no corresponding Article existed in the Declaration proposed by the Representative of Panama. The corresponding Article in the Declaration proposed by the United States was Article 5 (E/CN.4/36).

segments.speaker: BEGTRUP
segments.delegation: Commission on the Status of Women
segments.text: Mrs. BEGTRUP (Chairman of the Commission on the Status of Women) asked whether by prohibiting slavery "in all its forms" Article 11 was intended to cover the traffic in women. Would it not be preferable to mention this matter?

segments.speaker: AMADO
segments.text: Mr. AMADO (Panama) suggested the inclusion of this Article in the provisions of a Convention.

segments.speaker: CASSIN
segments.text: Mr. CASSIN (France) considered it impossible that a Declaration should make no mention of the prohibition of slavery. The text proposed by the Drafting Committee had in view human dignity, and in this general form it seemed to him to cover the prohibition of involuntary prostitution. He suggested the adoption, of this text, possibly with the addition of the second paragraph of Article 5 of the Declaration proposed by the United States.

segments.speaker: ROMULO
segments.text: Mr. ROMULO (Philippines) thought the second paragraph of the Article proposed by the United States could more appropriately be inserted in Article 10. He also proposed that in the English text of Article 11, the words "slavery which is" be replaced by "slavery being". His delegation preferred the text proposed by the Drafting Committee.
